exercises.paragraph: 3, 4, 5, and 6 Identify the surface with the given vector equation.

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{r}\left( {u,\upsilon} \right) = \left( {u + \upsilon} \right)\mathbf{i} + \left( {3 - \upsilon} \right)\mathbf{j} + \left( {1 + 4u + 5\upsilon} \right)\mathbf{k}$$

exercises.paragraph: 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, and 12 Use a computer to graph the parametric surface. Indicate on the graph which grid curves have $$u$$ constant and which have $$\upsilon$$ constant.

exercises.instruction: 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, and 18 Match the equations with the graphs labeled I–VI and give reasons for your answers. Determine which families of grid curves have $$u$$ constant and which have $$\upsilon$$ constant.

list.item: Details A grid curve is graphed in the x y z coordinate space. The positive x axis slopes down and to the left. The positive y axis slopes slightly down and to the right. The positive z axis runs vertically upward. Imagine a rectangular sheet with two longer sides along and parallel to the x axis. The midpoint of the side along the x-axis lies at the origin and a line parallel to its shorter sides lies along the positive y axis. The short sides of the sheet are folded upward and cross each other such that the vertical traces parallel to the x z plane resemble a drop at the bottom and a v shape at the top. The horizontal traces on the surface are lines perpendicular to the x z plane and parallel to the x y plane.

Details A grid curve is graphed in the x y z coordinate space. The positive x-axis slopes down and to the left. The positive y-axis slopes slightly down and to the right. The positive z axis runs vertically upward. Imagine a rectangular sheet curved like the outer surface of a right circular cylinder. The cylinder has its center at the origin. The left and right sides of the surface are squeezed together in the middle and fused along the x-axis. The horizontal traces parallel to the x y plane are circles and ellipses. The vertical traces are v-shaped curves with their vertices on the x axis.

Details A grid curve is graphed in the x y z coordinate space. The positive x-axis slopes down and to the left. The positive y-axis slopes slightly down and to the right. The positive z axis runs vertically upward. Imagine the grid curve to have two parts. The first part resembles a pyramid-shaped tent with its sides bulging inward. The second part is a reflection of the first part over the x y plane.

Details A grid curve is graphed in the x y z coordinate space. The positive x axis slopes down and to the left. The positive y axis slopes slightly down and to the right. The positive z axis runs vertically upward. Imagine a rectangular sheet with its left shorter side along the positive x axis. The back left corner of the rectangle is at the origin. The rectangle is curled around the positive y axis like a spiral incline. It begins with the rectangular plane's left side lying along the positive x axis and spirals upward, counterclockwise and completes two full revolutions.

Details A grid curve is graphed in the x y z coordinate space. The positive x axis slopes down and to the left. The positive y axis slopes slightly down and to the right. The positive z axis runs vertically upward. Imagine a curved pipe with its bottom end on the x z plane and the center of the circular mouth on the positive x axis. The pipe coils around the positive z axis twice and becomes progressively narrow as it climbs. Its top end meets the positive z axis.

Details A grid curve is graphed in the x y z coordinate space. The positive x axis runs horizontally leftward. The positive y axis slopes down and slightly to the right. The positive z axis runs vertically upward. Imagine a rectangular sheet lying on the x y plane with its center at the origin, shorter sides parallel to the x axis, and longer sides parallel to the y axis. The midpoints of the longer sides are brought upward and made to meet each other on the positive z axis. The shorter sides at the front and back open out from the fold on the z axis. Horizontal traces parallel to the x y plane and vertical traces parallel to the y z plane are drawn on the curved surface.

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{r}\left( {u,\upsilon} \right) = u\cos\upsilon\mathbf{i} + u\sin\upsilon\mathbf{j} + \upsilon\mathbf{k}$$
$$\mathbf{r}\left( {u,\upsilon} \right) = u\upsilon^{2}\mathbf{i} + u^{2}\upsilon\mathbf{j} + {({u^{2} - \upsilon^{2}})}\mathbf{k}$$
$$\mathbf{r}\left( {u,\upsilon} \right) = {({u^{3} - u})}\mathbf{i} + \upsilon^{2}\mathbf{j} + u^{2}\mathbf{k}$$
$$x = \left( {1 - u} \right)\left( {3 + \cos\upsilon} \right)\cos 4\pi u,$$
$$y = \left( {1 - u} \right)\left( {3 + \cos\upsilon} \right)\sin 4\pi u,$$
$$z = 3u + \left( {1 - u} \right)\sin\upsilon$$
$${x = \cos^{3}u\cos^{3}\upsilon},{y = \sin^{3}u\cos^{3}\upsilon},{z = \sin^{3}\upsilon}$$
$${x = \sin u},{y = \cos u\sin\upsilon},{z = \sin\upsilon}$$

exercises.paragraph: 27, and 28 Use a computer to produce a graph that looks like the given one.

image.alt: Details A grid curve is graphed in the x y z coordinate space. The axes are along three sides of a cubical box. The x axis is along the right side of the base and is displayed from negative 0 to 5, from back to front. The y axis is along the front side of the base and is displayed from negative 3 to 0, from left to right. The z axis is along the front side of the left face and is displayed from negative 3 to 3, from bottom to top. The curved surface resembles a vertical rectangular gridded sheet building back and to the left. The top side is along the right side of the top face of the box and the bottom side is along the x axis and the right side of the base. The longer sides of the surface bulge back and to the left such that their midpoints are on the z axis and on the midpoints of the front and back sides of the left face.

Details A grid curve is graphed in the x y z coordinate space. The axes are along three sides of a cubical box. The x axis is along the right side of the base and is displayed from negative 1 to 1, from back to front, in increments of 1. The y axis is along the front side of the base and is displayed from negative 1 to 1, from left to right, in increments of 1. The z axis is along the front side of the left face and is displayed from negative 1 to 1, from bottom to top, in increments of 1. The curved surface resembles a portion of a sphere with its top and a portion of its side facing the right edge of the front face cut off. Imagine a horizontal rectangular sheet with longer sides at the top and bottom. The bottom side is squeezed into a single point. The rest of the sheet is bent as if enveloping a sphere leaving out the top curved portion and almost a quarter of the sphere facing the right side of the ring face.

problem.paragraph: The surface with parametric equations
$$\begin{array}{rcl} x & = & {2\cos\theta + r\cos(\theta \slash 2)} \\ y & = & {2\sin\theta + r\cos(\theta \slash 2)} \\ z & = & {r\sin(\theta \slash 2)} \end{array}$$

problem.paragraph: The part of the plane $$3x + 2y + z = 6$$ that lies in the first octant

The part of the plane with vector equation $$\mathbf{r}\left( {u,\upsilon} \right) = {\langle{u + \upsilon,2 - 3u,1 + u - \upsilon}\rangle}$$ that is given by $$0 \leqslant u \leqslant 2$$ , $$- 1 \leqslant \upsilon \leqslant 1$$
The part of the plane $$x + 2y + 3z = 1$$ that lies inside the cylinder $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 3$$
The part of the cone $$z = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}$$ that lies between the plane $$y = x$$ and the cylinder $$y = x^{2}$$
The surface $$z = \frac{2}{3}{({x^{3 \slash 2} + y^{3 \slash 2}})}$$ , $$0 \leqslant x \leqslant 1$$ , $$0 \leqslant y \leqslant 1$$
The part of the surface $$z = 4 - 2x^{2} + y$$ that lies above the triangle with vertices $$\left( {0,0} \right)$$ , $$\left( {1,0} \right)$$ , and $$\left( {1,1} \right)$$
The part of the surface $$z = xy$$ that lies within the cylinder $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 1$$
The part of the surface $$x = z^{2} + y$$ that lies between the planes $$y = 0$$ , $$y = 2$$ , $$z = 0$$ , and $$z = 2$$
The part of the paraboloid $$y = x^{2} + z^{2}$$ that lies within the cylinder $$x^{2} + z^{2} = 16$$
The helicoid (or spiral ramp) with vector equation $$\mathbf{r}(u,v) = u\cos v\mathbf{i} + u\sin v\mathbf{j} + v\mathbf{k}$$ , $$0 \leqslant u \leqslant 1$$ , $$0 \leqslant \upsilon \leqslant \pi$$
The surface with parametric equations $$x = u^{2}$$ , $$y = u\upsilon$$ , $$z = \frac{1}{2}\upsilon^{2}$$ , $$0 \leqslant u \leqslant 1$$ , $$0 \leqslant \upsilon \leqslant 2$$

If the equation of a surface $$S$$ is $$z = f\left( {x,y} \right)$$ , where $$x^{2} + y^{2} \leqslant R^{2}$$ , and you know that $$\left| f_{x} \right| \leqslant 1$$ and $$\left| f_{y} \right| \leqslant 1$$ , what can you say about $$A(S)$$ ?

exercises.paragraph: 52–53 Find the area of the surface correct to four decimal places by first simplifying an expression for area to one in terms of a single integral and then evaluating the integral numerically.

problem.paragraph: The part of the surface $$z = \cos{({x^{2} + y^{2}})}$$ that lies inside the cylinder $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 1$$
The part of the surface $$z = \ln{({x^{2} + y^{2} + 2})}$$ that lies above the disk $$x^{2} + y^{2} \leqslant 1$$

Use a computer algebra system to find, to four decimal places, the area of the part of the surface $$z = {({1 + x^{2}})} \slash {({1 + y^{2}})}$$ that lies above the square $$|x| + |y| \leqslant 1$$ . Illustrate by graphing this part of the surface.

list.item: Use the Midpoint Rule for double integrals (see Section 15.1) with six squares to estimate the area of the surface $$z = 1 \slash {({1 + x^{2} + y^{2}})}$$ , $$0 \leqslant x \leqslant 6$$ , $$0 \leqslant y \leqslant 4$$ .
Use a computer algebra system to approximate the surface area in part (a) to four decimal places. Compare with the answer to part (a).

problem.paragraph: Use a computer algebra system to find the area of the surface with vector equation $$\mathbf{r}(u,v) = {\langle{\cos^{3}u\cos^{3}v,\sin^{3}u\cos^{3}v,\sin^{3}v}\rangle}$$ , $$0 \leqslant u \leqslant \pi$$ , $$0 \leqslant v \leqslant 2\pi$$ . State your answer correct to four decimal places.
Use a computer algebra system to find the exact area of the surface $$z = 1 + 2x + 3y + 4y^{2}$$ , $$1 \leqslant x \leqslant 4$$ , $$0 \leqslant y \leqslant 1$$ .

list.item: Set up, but do not evaluate, a double integral for the area of the surface with parametric equations $$x = au\cos\upsilon$$ , $$y = bu\sin\upsilon$$ , $$z = u^{2}$$ , $$0 \leqslant u \leqslant 2$$ , $$0 \leqslant \upsilon \leqslant 2\pi$$ .

For the case $$a = 2$$ , $$b = 3$$ , use a computer algebra system to find the surface area correct to four decimal places.

problem.paragraph: Find the area of the part of the sphere $$x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = 4z$$ that lies inside the paraboloid $$z = x^{2} + y^{2}$$ .
